set.body:
Objective:
Create a typed request-compile-resolve seam from scheduler-neutral Sojourn submissions to durable concrete scala-slurm requests, then use the same resource model for batch and leased pilot pools.

Scope:
1. Stabilize the current artifact and managed-lifecycle foundation without duplicating SCOMP.6 or S3.
2. Introduce TaskSubmission, portable ExecutionRequirements, PlacementClass, and typed planning rejection.
3. Introduce scala-slurm JobIntent to SiteProfile resolution to durable ResolvedJobRequest.
4. Implement SlurmRequestCompiler plus an explicit advanced Slurm submission lane.
5. Add homogeneous pilot capacity, task-fit admission, Slurm pool wiring, and pool artifact parity.

Design constraints:
- Start with an honest SingleProcess execution shape; do not expose portable nodes, ranks, tasks, or MPI until the worker protocol implements them.
- Resource requirements are scheduling and admission requirements, not claims of runtime usage enforcement.
- Unsupported requirements are rejected as data and are never silently ignored.
- Resource or placement changes participate in submission conflict identity.
- Site defaults are resolved before durable admission so retries cannot drift with later configuration changes.

Completion criteria:
- All child slices are closed.
- Batch and pool accept the same TaskSubmission contract.
- scala-slurm records requested intent and the concrete effective request used for replay.
- Local, CLI Slurm, and SSH Slurm behavior is covered by focused tests and applicable TCK laws.
- Pool tasks exceeding pilot capacity never execute.
- No provider type crosses into sojourn-core.
set.title: EPIC: Add sound execution planning and resource-aware pools
